Phenols are compounds that have a hydroxyl group (-OH) directly attached to an aromatic ring. The simplest phenol is C6H5OH, which consists of a benzene ring with an -OH group attached.

Cresols are methylphenols - they are phenols with a methyl group (-CH3) attached to the aromatic ring. The key functional group that characterizes both phenols and cresols is still the hydroxyl group (-OH).
